user-round-cog.reason: Fixed 300 ms easeOut group rotation to 180 degrees, hold completion and current-pose scalar replay fit the cycle adapter. Deferred until half-turn decomposition, interrupted return and payload are measured.

wifi-sync.reason: Entry rotates the group through -360 degrees. A computed matrix loses completed turns; return must retain the unwrapped angle. No replacement has proved this behavior.

key-square.reason: Finite rotate and scale tracks share timing, but the cycle adapter supports one transform property. Preserve transform order and independent current values before migration.

wallet.reason: Finite y and rotate keyframes have explicit entry/return timing. Combined transform interpolation and current-pose replay need a separate capability and proof.

key-circle.reason: Finite y and rotate arrays have different lengths. Each property needs its own offsets before transforms can be composed faithfully.

cart.reason: Return continues the interrupted y sampler while scale returns independently; y repeats and has a property delay.

snowflake.reason: Finite rotation entry returns with a stiffness 500/damping 25 spring that inherits interrupted angular velocity.

key.reason: Rotation returns with a stiffness 120/damping 14 spring and retained angular velocity.

refresh-cw-off.reason: Finite x shake returns with a stiffness 500/damping 20 spring and retained velocity.

phone.reason: Rotation and scale have distinct velocity-dependent spring return settings.

phone-call.reason: Rotation and scale return through distinct springs, combined with the signal mechanism on child paths.

phone-forwarded.reason: SVG pulse and child transforms use different velocity-dependent spring returns.

badge-alert.reason: Scale and rotation use distinct keyframe arrays and velocity-dependent spring returns.

cursor-click.reason: Timed multitransform entry combines delayed opacity. Scalar x/y normal poses have no duration and inherit svg-parts spring defaults.

eye.reason: Finite opacity runs on path and circle alongside scaleY and scale. Opacity support alone does not cover transform replay and return.

cpu.reason: Pins combine opacity and axis-dependent scale with repeated entry tracks. Repeat boundaries and interruption need separate proof.

keyboard.reason: Each playback samples Math.random for per-key delays and clears immediately on return. A static timed sequence would change the recipe.

airplay.reason: Entry queues a path reveal and triangle transform phase followed by return; interruption cancels queued phases.
